alert.trigger: This alert triggers when the green and blue systems pressure ≤1 450 PSI (the alert resets if pressure ≥1 750 PSI).

effectivity.note: One FCOM procedure for all HS-TX. Only the QRH fuel penalty factor differs (see HS-TX differences).

summary: A red warning with red LAND ASAP: green and blue hydraulics are lost. The FCTM says a MAYDAY should be declared, and the ECAM actions should be completed before the approach. No AP, alternate law with protections lost, no slats and no ailerons, only the right elevator. It is a hand-flown approach with selected speed and A/THR off, flap lever 3, and a gravity gear extension at 200 kt, which gives direct law. Use the QRH summary after the ECAM.

background.text: Dual hydraulic failures bring loss of the AP, flight control law degradation, landing in an abnormal configuration, extensive ECAM procedures and significant considerations for approach and landing.
Pitch: with HYD G+B, alternate law has no protections; direct law applies in roll.
The RAT can be extended at any time with the RAT MAN ON pushbutton.

technique.text: A double hydraulic failure is an emergency, with red LAND ASAP displayed; a MAYDAY should be declared. Land as soon as possible, but complete the ECAM actions before the approach.
It is a "complex procedure": refer to the QRH summary when the ECAM procedure is complete. A clear reading of STATUS is essential to sequence the actions during the approach.
The PF is very busy flying and communicating in alternate law. Handling may differ because some control surfaces are lost, so maneuver with care.
The G+B approach extends the gear at 200 kt: below 200 kt direct law gives better pitch control than alternate law with one elevator and all slats lost.

gaps.text: The FCTM and PDP give the sequence but no PF/PM slide for this failure: the turns come from the AOP-20 task sharing, FCTM AOP-30-60 and the QRH summary. The manuals do not say who turns the handcrank; the PM is shown from instructor practice.
The DSC does not label the RAT MAN ON pushbutton as guarded, so no crosscheck is shown for it; the BLUE ELEC PUMP pb is labelled guarded.
The MAYDAY wording is not given in the supplied manuals.
